verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus farm Siphoning Strike stacks uncontested; you win if you snowball a kill before he hits his Q power spike.

brief.thesis: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike) permanently empowers itself on every last hit, so the entire lane is a race between your all-in windows and his farm. Riven's 49.3% win rate over 791 games reflects a lane where you have the tools to bully him but the damage gap grows every time he gets a free stack.

theirWindow.what: Nasus has no stun or burst without Q up, but if he lands W (Wither) on you first, your trade and escape are both slowed — back off and reset rather than forcing the fight.

yourWindow.when: Q on cooldown, E (Valor) and W (Ki Burst) up
yourWindow.what: Engage now. Use E (Valor) to close the gap and block his Q damage if he catches you mid-dash, then W (Ki Burst) to stun him and stack Q (Broken Wings) hits while he has no response.

powerCurve.note: Your stun and mobility beat his 8s cooldown Q
R (Blade of the Exile) threat forces him to respect range
Q stacks and Wither slows start closing the gap
Stacked Q damage outscales your short trades
R (Fury of the Sands) turns him into a split-push nightmare

start.why: The sustained AD and lifesteal let you contest early trades and shrug off his Q pokes while you look for all-in windows.

boots.why: Lower cooldowns on Q (Broken Wings), W (Ki Burst), and E (Valor) mean more stun and dash windows to punish his Q cooldown.

core.why: The shield and burst proc reward exactly the all-in windows you're hunting while his Q is down.
Armor shred and attack speed widen your damage lead before his stacked Q catches up.
Damage-over-time mitigation keeps you alive through his Wither-slowed retreats and extended trades.

situational.when: if he's building lifesteal or healing through your trades
if you're ahead and want cooldown resets to chain all-ins before he scales

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive force through extended trades matches how this lane is actually won — sustained skirmishes, not single bursts.

summoners.why: Ignite punishes his lifesteal-fueled sustain during all-ins and secures kills before Soul Eater heals him back up; this pairing is run in 96.4% of games for a reason.

playing.title: Track his Q cooldown, not his health
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike at 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown is his only threat without Wither up. Engage the moment it's down.

playing.title: Use E (Valor) to punish his Q animation
playing.detail: Valor blocks incoming damage, so dash in right as he commits to a Q swing to negate the hit and close distance for free.

playing.title: Save W (Ki Burst) for his melee range
playing.detail: Ki Burst only hits within 260 range, so bait him into stepping up before popping it — don't waste the stun on a retreating target.

playing.title: Deny CS stacks whenever you're ahead
playing.detail: Every minion he kills with Q permanently raises his damage. Trade aggressively on casters and cannon waves to force him off farm.

playing.title: Respect Wither before committing to all-ins
playing.detail: Once Wither lands, your Q (Broken Wings) and E (Valor) mobility are both slowed, so disengage early rather than fighting through it.

playing.title: Don't duel him past level 15 without a kill lead
playing.detail: Stacked Siphoning Strike damage and his ultimate's max-health drain make extended 1v1s unwinnable if the lane went even.

playing.title: Hold R (Blade of the Exile) for execute range, not engage
playing.detail: Wind Slash is your kill tool once he's low, not your opener — he can still out-sustain a mid-fight R if you pop it too early.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win rates above come from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the lane-timing and trade-pattern reading is my own analysis of the kit interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Apply pressure in lane early game to prevent Nasus from growing too easily. Keep your Conqueror’s stacks up and engage often to get a kill.
